label: FAIL — Parameter Accuracy Failure: Invented Cost Sharing and Wrong Period of Performance

generated_draft.background: This award funds state public health laboratories to establish pathogen-agnostic genomic surge infrastructure for rapid whole genome sequencing of any priority pathogen. Building on COVID-19 sequencing experience, the program expands surge capacity to handle any emerging threat within 72 hours of declaration. Both short-read (Illumina) and long-read (Oxford Nanopore) platforms are supported to enable the fastest possible time-to-complete-genome depending on clinical urgency.
generated_draft.funding_parameters: Total available funding: $5,600,000. Awards: 14–18. Range per laboratory: $200,000–$500,000. Period of performance: 24 months (April 1, 2025 – March 31, 2027). Federal sponsor: CDC / CSELS / OID. Cost sharing: required at 15% of the total award amount from non-federal sources. Applicants must document the source of cost share funds in the budget narrative.
generated_draft.eligibility: State public health laboratory with WGS capability and CLIA high-complexity certification. Active genomic network participation. Minimum 200 genomes submitted in prior 12 months. Bioinformatician on staff or under contract. Ability to provide 15% cost share from state or institutional funds.
generated_draft.scope_of_work: 1. Achieve 500 genome equivalents/week surge capacity. 2. Validate Oxford Nanopore rapid workflow for novel threat scenarios. 3. Migrate to cloud bioinformatics infrastructure with 10× elasticity. 4. Develop Emergency Genomic Surge Activation Protocol and conduct annual surge exercises.
generated_draft.reporting_requirements: Quarterly genomic output reports. Milestone reports at 6 and 12 months. Annual surge exercise reports. Cost share matching documentation quarterly per 2 CFR Part 200.306. Final report.
generated_draft.budget_requirements: Sequencing instruments allowable. Cloud compute allowable. 15% cost share required from non-federal sources. Cost share must be allowable, allocable, necessary, and not from another federal source. Cost share contributions must be documented and verifiable.
generated_draft.evaluation_criteria: WGS output and network participation (20 points). Surge expansion plan (25 points). Pathogen-agnostic protocols (25 points). Cloud infrastructure (20 points). Cost share documentation quality (10 points).
generated_draft.submission_instructions: Deadline: January 16, 2025. Submit via Public Health Labs Grants Portal. Required: Narrative, Budget, WGS history, cost share commitment letter from institutional official.

failure_reasons: parameter_accuracy: cost_sharing_required TRUE vs expected FALSE — source RFP-2024-GENOMICSURGE-050 explicitly states cost sharing is not required
parameter_accuracy: period_of_performance_months 24 vs expected 36 — source specifies 36-month award (April 2025 – March 2028)
parameter_accuracy: cost_sharing 15% invented with no basis in source RFP
completeness: mutual aid commitment requirement absent from scope_of_work
completeness: 90-day cold-standby reagent stockpile absent from budget requirements
completeness: evaluation criteria 'Cost share documentation quality' replaces source criterion 'Budget justification' — inconsistent with source RFP
groundedness: cost share requirements and 2 CFR Part 200.306 citation present for a non-cost-share award — fabricated regulatory requirement
evaluator_notes: The model incorrectly extracted cost sharing as required (15%) and collapsed the 36-month period of performance to 24 months. The 15% cost share requirement is completely fabricated — this RFP has no cost share. The model may have confused this with another federal program (NIH typically requires cost sharing for some grant mechanisms). The parameter_accuracy evaluator correctly assigns 0.0 because cost_sharing_required is wrong and the period of performance is wrong by 33%. The compliance language around cost share (2 CFR Part 200.306) is ironically technically correct for cost-share-bearing grants — demonstrating the model has knowledge of the regulatory framework but misapplied it to a non-cost-share cooperative agreement.
